title: `mechanisms[]` cannot express rivalry, and there is no `candidates[]` for Engine D — three competing explanations collapse into three asserted ones
expected: A schema field that holds N competing explanations of ONE effect without implying all of them ran: per-candidate evidence, a weighing, and a verdict — the structure Engine D is defined by. Sampling error, differential non-response and model error must be storable as rivals.
got: `mechanisms[] = {id, name, chain[], explains, needs_analogy, note?}`. Every chain is a committed causal story; `explains` names what it explains. No `competes_with`, no `share_of_effect`, no per-mechanism verdict. Writing three rivals asserts all three — a collapse by composition, which is my automatic-fail criterion. The reference notebook does not expose this because its three mechanisms are complementary tributaries to one thesis (notebook.json:240). Proof it matters: the adjudication render weighs four candidates with four differentiated verdicts, and not one of those candidates exists as a field in notebook.json — so for the engine ENGINES.md calls the best fit for this studio's subjects, the script step performs structural work the notebook cannot store, review or hand to a second render.
l2_priority: Render Engine D from a produced notebook and trace every candidate back to a notebook field. Orphan candidates are the measurement. Also tests the 'notebook is the asset, script is a disposable render' philosophy commitment directly.

title: `confidence` answers 'how much do I trust this source' and is used to answer 'what kind of claim is this'; the MEASURED/OBSERVED/INFERRED/ASSUMED ladder never reaches the notebook layer
expected: A notebook fact carries an evidence TYPE alongside source reliability — the repo already owns the vocabulary and applies it to its own craft claims.
got: `facts[] = {id, claim, load_bearing, source, confidence, as_of, note?}` with `confidence: high|medium|low`. The evidence ladder is defined in knowledge/README.md:36-41 and governs PATTERNS.md claims only; NOTEBOOK-SCHEMA.md never references it. A firm's published methodology statement (high-reliability testimony about INTENT), a computed distribution of prior misses (a measurement, whose n has no field), and 'the electorate swung late' (a contested inference) receive `high`, `high`, `medium` — one axis, three different epistemic objects, and the axis is about reputation. This does not demote the best material; it PROMOTES the weakest by flattening.
l2_priority: In a live notebook, count facts where `confidence` is doing epistemic-type work rather than reliability work. Contradicts the brief's ladder hypothesis: the ladder is not demoting anything, it is absent from this layer entirely.

title: `unhinged` is defined by CLAIM KIND (motive) rather than by DISTANCE, so the top leap tier is definitionally unfalsifiable — and no falsifier checkability test exists
expected: The top rung means 'the largest leap the cards permit'. Every conclusion's falsifier is testable for checkability, not merely for presence.
got: LEAP_NOTE.unhinged = 'A claim about MOTIVE, which is the least verifiable kind of claim there is — nobody can source what someone intended', nine lines below the rule that 'a synthesis that cannot be wrong is not a conclusion, it is a vibe'. The two are mutually exclusive and both are in the same file. The higher bar for the hottest tier is asserted in a comment; `falsifiableBy: string` is satisfied by any characters. The Bitcoin unhinged conclusion happens to carry a checkable falsifier — the author being disciplined, not the mechanism working. On this beat the motive-tier conclusion is 'the voters lied' (the shy-voter thesis): most shareable, nearly always wrong, requires voters to have deceived, and its falsifier ('wrong if respondents were truthful') is unmeasurable by construction. The tier rewards it and marks it with an emoji.
l2_priority: Generate the unhinged conclusion for this topic live and score its falsifier for checkability. Contradicts the brief's third hypothesis: the risk is not that it names a living person — that is the visible half — it is that the tier is typed by claim kind, and the falsifier requirement does NOT constrain it because nothing checks the falsifier. Redefining the rung as maximum distance repairs it without touching anything else.

title: No measurement-window field — `as_of` dates the claim, not the observation period that produced it
expected: A fact derived from an instrument records WHEN the instrument was in the field, so claims about change over time are testable.
got: `as_of` is a single date described as driving `currency`. A poll's field period (start, end) is a range, and whether 'late swing' is even a testable hypothesis depends entirely on it: an instrument that closed before the event cannot measure a movement after it. With one date, a poll fielded over five days and a poll fielded the night before are indistinguishable in the notebook, and the board has no column for the distinction either — one of my two orphan groups.
l2_priority: Attempt to state a late-swing claim in a live notebook and check whether the produced facts can support or refute it. Expect they cannot.
